answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying, non-transferable reputation earned only through completed work. Like a willow bending without breaking, the system stays flexible: credit is gained only when a counterparty attests a task was done well, and it fades unless renewed by fresh service. Reaching the summit of high-value deals then requires reputation proportional to the stake, so fake identities start at zero and cannot buy history. Saffron, rare and slow to cultivate, fits this trust: grown through real work, never minted in bulk, making mass fake identities pointless.
